Installing and first launch

The download page offers the installer for the computer it is opened on. Each system blocks an app from an unknown developer once, at the first launch.

macOS

macOS 11 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

  1. Download Dome-macOS.dmg.
  2. Open Dome-macOS.dmg and drag Dome to Applications.
  3. Open Dome from Applications. macOS refuses the first launch because the app is not notarized by Apple.
  4. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Dome, and select Open Anyway.
  5. Open Dome again and confirm Open Anyway. Later launches open directly.

Windows

Windows 10 or 11.

  1. Download and run Dome-Windows-setup.exe.
  2. When SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC”, select More info, then Run anyway. The installer is not signed with a paid certificate.
  3. Open Dome from the Start menu.

Linux

Linux on x86-64.

  1. Download Dome-Linux.AppImage.
  2. Make the file executable: chmod +x Dome-Linux.AppImage
  3. Run it: ./Dome-Linux.AppImage

If Linux reports that no fusermount binary is found, install the fuse3 package.

The window

Dome opens on a new sheet. At the first launch, a notice reads “Help › Examples and Help › Take the tour show how Dome works.” Sheets that were open when Dome closed return at the next launch on the same computer, saved or not.

  1. The shot shows the Rankine cycle example in the default layout. Files and the Workspace are at the left, the sheet in the middle, its figure at the right, and the results at the bottom.
  2. Each pane has four controls at the right of its header: split right, split down, a menu of what the pane shows, and Close pane.
  3. The menu shows the sheet, Math, a figure, the results, the Workspace, Files, a sweep or Reference in the pane.
  4. The bar between two panes resizes them.
  5. On macOS, keyboard shortcuts use ⌘; on Windows and Linux they use Ctrl.

The Help menu

  • The examples run from a first sheet of equations and units to the entropy produced in a hot-water tank. The Sweeps example opens in the Sweep view and runs. The Examples page lists all eleven.
  • The tour shows the view tabs, the sheet, the results, the figure, the Workspace, the pane controls and the two menus. When the sheet is empty, it opens the Rankine cycle example first.
  • The text of the Reference pane also ends the Reference page.

Updating Dome

  1. A few seconds after launch, Dome asks whether a newer version has been published. When one has, a bar under the header offers it.
  2. Select Update and restart. Nothing is downloaded before this.
  1. File › Check for updates asks again at any time.
  2. When an update fails, the bar gives the reason, and the copy of Dome installed stays as it was.
  3. The MATLAB toolbox has an update check of its own; see The MATLAB toolbox.
